$comment: THE COURSE MANIFEST — the one place that says what content exists.
Nothing in src/ names a course, a unit or a graph file. src/content/index.js
reads this file, resolves the graphs beside it, loads the generator packs the
units name, and hands the engine a graph. Adding Algebra II, Geometry or
Trigonometry is: write a graph, write a pack, add a block here.
See content/COURSES.md for the full walk-through.
FIELDS
courses[].id        stable id; used in the save and in ?course=
courses[].titleKey  i18n key for the course name (src/i18n)
courses[].status    'shipped' | 'preview' | 'planned'
courses[].frameworks which standards frameworks its nodes cite
units[].id          stable id; used in ?unit= and names the graph file
units[].graph       path, relative to content/, of the unit's graph
units[].pack        generator pack module id, or null for the core bank
units[].requires    unit ids whose nodes this unit's prereqs may point at
default names the unit a player gets when nothing asks for anything else.
It must never change without a migration: it is the shipped experience.
THE ROUTE. default.unit is where a learner STARTS, not where they stop.
route names the course a player walks with no query string, and units
opens in sequence along it: a unit is open once every line of every unit
it requires is held. Opening is one-way — a line that lapses reopens the
line, never the region. src/content/index.js does the reading; nothing
else in src/ names a course. With a cleared save exactly one unit is open,
so a new learner gets byte-for-byte the shipped ten-node lattice.
route.course   the course the route walks
route.units    the units it may reach, in course order, or null for
every unit the manifest itself calls status: shipped.
A unit that is not on the route is still reachable by
?unit= / ?course=; it is simply never put in front of a
learner who did not ask for it.
WHY THE ROUTE STOPS AT LEVEL 2, AND WHAT MOVES IT.
The route is named outright rather than derived from status because a
region a learner walks into has to be measured on the lattice the route
actually composes, not on the unit alone. Re-measured today,
tools/simulate.mjs, 300 learners, 3600-item budget:
node tools/simulate.mjs 300 3600 --units algebra1-l1,algebra1-l2
-> 98.0% true mastery; a knower proves the whole lattice 58.0% of
the time, 175 min median
node tools/simulate.mjs 300 3600 --units algebra1-l1,algebra1-l2,algebra1-l3
-> 64.0% true mastery; a knower proves it 2.3% of the time
The third one misses the 80% promise this product is held to by sixteen
points, so Level 3 is not put in front of anybody yet. Get that to 80%
and add the unit id to route.units below and set its status back to
shipped. That is the whole change: the loader, the world, the session and
the narrative all read this list.
STATUS AND ROUTE MUST AGREE, and they did not.
algebra1-l3 said status: shipped while the route stopped at Level 2, so
the manifest was claiming a unit was in the product that no player could
ever be handed. tools/critic/reachable.mjs read that claim and failed on
it, correctly. `shipped` in this file means PUT IN FRONT OF A LEARNER —
it is what routeUnits() falls back on when route.units is null, and it is
what the reachability gate asserts. A finished unit that the route does
not walk to is `preview`: on disk, validated by check:courses and
check:mastery exactly as before, reachable with ?unit= / ?course=, and
never put in front of somebody who did not ask for it. Nothing about
Level 3 is unfinished except the number above.
